static_traits.name: Zhou Ting
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends and family are strained by their excessive focus on weight; has one close friend but has not yet shared their physical and emotional struggles
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological issues before; has not yet received psychotherapy/counseling
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, can reflect on own feelings, emotions mainly Anxiety, highly cooperative, Positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I feel overwhelmed worrying that I will always be overweight, even though I have only lost 5 pounds; this has caused ongoing stress and Anxiety over the past few months, especially noticeable After meals, when looking in the mirror, or weighing myself.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent negative thoughts about weight and appearance have already affected mental health and daily function; I hope to learn to manage these thoughts through counseling, so as to feel better.
growth_experiences: After starting a new diet plan a few months ago, comments from others about weight triggered intense focus on body shape; over time Anxiety worsened, with multiple weigh-ins daily, repeated Self-denial After meals and when looking in the mirror, and gradually avoiding food-related socializing, with eating patterns becoming disordered.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on weight and appearance
If I do not see significant results in the short term, it means I cannot do it and nothing will change

special_situations.event: Seeing no obvious change or only a small drop in the numbers when weighing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If weight has not dropped quickly and noticeably, it means losing weight is hopeless and I will always be fat
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Weighs herself frequently to seek certainty and strengthen control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I only lost 5 pounds; I will always be fat.

special_situations.event: Focusing on body shape after meals or when looking in the mirror
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as I see any 'flaw', it proves I have failed at losing weight
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding food-related social occasions, tightening diet to avoid 'making mistakes'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I look terrible; that means I have failed.

special_situations.event: Recalling others' comments about one's weight
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If no one comments on my weight, it means I am not accepted and they are negating me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Not confiding in friends, Reduced socializing to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must think I am very fat and undisciplined.

special_situations.event: Realizing they have only lost about 5 pounds
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only significant, rapid weight loss counts as success; nothing else is worth affirming
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating existing progress, increasing self Demands and control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: 5 pounds is not progress at all.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and recognized, hoping to gain a sense of value and security by controlling the body and appearance
core_conflict.fear: Fears being evaluated, humiliated, and rejected; worries about losing control and being seen as a failure
defense_goal: Using self-criticism and high standards to prevent Being rejected or shame
Keeping a safe distance by Avoids socializing and not disclosing vulnerability
Using the sense of control over weight numbers to ease inner unease

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When facing or anticipating others' comments about their weight/appearance (e.g., group meals, meeting people)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will judge and reject me like reviewers (projecting inner harsh criticism onto others through transference)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use vague and avoidant expressions, reduce self-disclosure, cautious tone, deflecting to neutral topics like 'busy lately/not very hungry'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others affirm positive changes such as losing 5 pounds
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: This positive information is not reliable or 'has no meaning', and needs to be measured against stricter standards
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasize with numbers and rules that it is 'not real progress', flat tone, avoid talking about emotional experience, refute positive feedback with data.

manifestations: Has not yet shared their troubles with close friends due to shame
Avoiding food-related social activities, Relationship tension and drifting apart
Feeling trapped and isolated about weight issues
outcomes: Insufficient use of social support, emotional Lack of support

manifestations: Dominated by weight numbers and external evaluations; the space for inner choice and experience is compressed
Constrains himself with the value condition 'must be thin to count as good'
Pursues a sense of control through frequent weighing and strict diet control
outcomes: Compulsive monitoring (weighing multiple times) and disordered eating

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Using body weight numbers and others' evaluations as the core standard of self-worth
Negating positive changes like 'losing 5 pounds', believing they 'do not count as success'
Insisting on the rule that 'one must be thin to be good / to be worth accepting'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Blaming oneself: 'if I cannot even lose weight, other areas will fail too'
Worrying about 'being a burden to friends' and thus not asking for help, excessively restraining self-expression
Cautious when interacting with people, avoids exposing vulnerability and shame

positive_force: Help-seeking motivation is clear, attitude is positive, willing to try cognitive restructuring (de-catastrophizing)
Able to persist with certain diet and exercise attempts, has achieved about 5 pounds of objective progress
Has potential social support resources (has a close friend he is willing to trust)
Can notice trigger situations (After meals, looking in the mirror, weighing) and express inner experience
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases: catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and negating the positive
Tightly binding self-worth to weight and appearance, forming a rigid standard
A problem-maintaining behavior cycle of weighing multiple times daily, avoiding food-related socializing, etc.
Shame and high sensitivity to others' evaluations reduce access to help and support
Overly high expectations of short-term results lead to frustration and helplessness

target_behavior.behavior: Weighing themselves multiple times daily and monitoring weight
antecedent: Focusing on body shape when looking in the mirror
When Anxiety about weight and appearance rises
target_behavior.core_reason: Gaining a sense of control and certainty by monitoring numbers, to ease catastrophic anticipation ('if it does not drop I will be fat forever')
target_behavior.function: Relieving Anxiety in the short term, gaining temporary certainty and security
target_behavior.consequence: Reinforcing dependence on numbers and the Anxiety cycle, emotional setbacks that worsen Self-denial, affecting daily life

antecedent: When thinking of being judged on body shape at a gathering
Receiving social invitations involving group meals
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing judgment and shame, projecting inner harsh criticism into others' gazes
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluation and uncomfortable emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships drifting apart and Increased sense of isolation, Fewer opportunities to gain social support

target_behavior.behavior: Disordered eating patterns (frequently switching between different diet/exercise plans)
antecedent: Feeling disappointed or anxious after weighing
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization lead to catastrophizing interpretations of short-term fluctuations, eager to regain control through new plans
target_behavior.function: Seeks a quick and effective sense of control and 'success'
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty forming stable healthy eating habits, further intensifying frustration and Anxiety
